title: Demand elasticity trigger rules and HC flex protocol
content:
SUMMARY:
Objective: Produce a compact, operational playbook tying price changes to headcount and capacity responses. This doc contains: a baseline 12-month budget extract, three demand scenarios with pricing sensitivity, phased headcount plan by role, and a set of explicit trigger rules (metrics + thresholds) to move between hiring/capacity actions.

CONTEXT:
- Prior work: Q2 pricing experiments, FY27 mid-year reforecast. CFO asked for a lightweight mechanism to \u201ctranslate\u201d revenue delta into hiring and capacity actions with fast decision rules.
- Constraints: Must preserve service SLAs (99.9% API uptime, median gen latency target <= 120ms for standard tier) and preferred minimum gross margin of 45% on hosted API product.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS (base case):
- Base price per 1k input+output tokens: $0.38 (hosted API generation).
- Embedding unit price: $0.005 per 1k dims-equivalent call.
- Average token consumption per call: 350 tokens.
- Monthly active paying customers (MAU paying) baseline: 8,400.
- Annual churn assumed stable at 4.8% monthly (cohort projection baked into revenue forecast).
- Average engineer fully-loaded cost: $210k/year; SRE/infra: $240k/year; Sales/CS average: $150k/year.
- Cloud GPU cost blended (vm + gpu + networking): $0.80 per 1k tokens in base utilization.
- Cache/batching improvements scheduled in Q1 will reduce per-token infra cost by 10% vs base.

Notes: Revenue is net of discounts and partner share; model compute is the direct per-token cost including dedicated pool premiums. Headcount cost includes hire phasing (~+6 hires across FY).

HEADCOUNT PHASING (recommended hires and timing):
Role,Count,Hire window,Justification,Trigger (metric)
Senior Backend Engineer,2,Q1(Q1-2027),Improve batching and KV cache throughput,API 95th latency > 240ms for 14 days
SRE/Infra Engineer,2,Q2(Q2-2027),Dedicated pool ops and autoscaler work,Hosted capacity utilization > 75% and SLA error budget consumption > 30%
Solutions Eng (mid),1,Q3(Q3-2027),Support enterprise Dedicated ramp,Committed Dedicated contracts >= $150k ARR
Cost Analytics / Pricing PM,1,Q1-Q2,Coordinate price experiments and revenue telemetry,Abnormal revenue intensity (MoM change) > +/- 12%
Contract GPU Ops (fractional),0.5,On-demand,Short-term burst support,Spikes in model-queue wait time > 30s

PRICING SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (3 scenarios vs base):
Scenario A: Price cut 10% (to $0.342 / 1k tokens) + demand uplift +18%
- Revenue effect: +6.4% (elasticity partial offset; uplift concentrated in self-serve accounts)
- Model compute effect: +18% volume * slightly better amortization => compute spend +12%
- Net margin: compresses 6ppt vs base; still > 38% but below preferred 45%
- Hiring impact: defer two backend hires from Q1 to Q2; delay Solutions Eng hire until commit observed

Scenario B: Price increase 12% (to $0.4256 / 1k tokens) + demand drop -8%
- Revenue effect: +3.2% (price increases offset by volume loss)
- Compute spend: -6% due to lower volume
- Net margin: expands ~4-5ppt; headcount capacity slack appears (utilization drops by ~9%)
- Hiring impact: postpone SRE hires by one quarter; move funds to retention/compensation adjustments in sales

Scenario C: Cost shock (GPU spot market +40%) with no price change
- Revenue effect: unchanged
- Compute spend: +40% -> margin collapse unless mitigated by quant/quantization or routing
- Short-term mitigations: enable quantized serving on 30% of traffic, aggressive prefix cache fallbacks, restrict large-batch low-priority jobs to Dedicated overflow
- Hiring impact: freeze all non-critical hiring and reallocate 1 headcount budget to contractor GPU ops to manage transient peaks

SENSITIVITY SUMMARY (table of deltas vs base):
Metric,Price -10%,Price +12%,GPU+40%
Revenue,-6.4%*,+3.2%,0%
ModelCompute,+12%,-6%,+40%
GrossMargin,-6ppt,+5ppt,-18ppt
HiringAction,Delay hires by ~1 quarter,Postpone SRE hires by 1 quarter,Hiring freeze + contract ops
* uplift in users partially offsets price cut, net revenue still nuanced by churn and ARPA changes

TRIGGER RULES (explicit operational signals):
1) Hiring triggers (finance + hiring ops):
   - If trailing 6-month ARR net new adds > $1.2M and gross margin >= 43% then approve +1 net new engineer hire (backend/SRE).
   - If committed Dedicated ARR >= $150k and conversion probability >= 60% then approve Solutions Engineer hire and +$40k quota for SE ramp.

2) Capacity scaling triggers (infra/SRE):
   - If average GPU pool utilization > 78% for 7 consecutive days OR queued model requests > 120s median then open autoscale/provision +20% capacity and notify finance (cost run rate up).
   - If API 95th latency breaches 240ms for 14 days AND error budget drawdown > 30% then prioritize low-latency kernel paths and order hardware/burst capacity.

3) Pricing experiment rollback rules (product + finance):
   - If a price change (up or down) yields MoM revenue change outside +/-12% or causes MAU churn increase > 2ppt within 30 days, revert to prior price and run A/B segmented analysis.

OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK (actions & owners):
- Finance (owner: Leah O'Connor): weekly report extract of revenue, margin, utilization; maintain rolling 12-week hiring runway table.
- Product Pricing (owner: Nora Kim): run controlled rollouts, track cohort responses, forward results to finance biweekly.
- Infra/SRE (owner: Evan Park): maintain capacity dashboards, runback autoscaling tests, produce incident retros for any SLA breach tied to capacity.
- Recruiting (shared): maintain 8-week candidate pipeline for critical roles flagged by triggers.

ESCALATION PATH (fast lanes):
- If margin compression > 8ppt MoM due to compute cost: CFO + Head of Infra + Head of Product meet within 48 hours to sign emergency mitigations (pricing tests or temporary job scheduling limits).
- If sustained SLA exposure (error budget > 50% draw) for > 72 hours: SRE runbook -> paging -> exec standup.

CHECKLIST (pre-commit review for hires when trigger fired):
- Confirm 6-month ARR growth and margin metrics (finance extract)
- Cost of hire and ramp model (finance + hiring ops)
- On-call and project capacity plan from team (manager)
- Candidate pipeline confirmation (recruiting)

ANNEX: QUICK CALC SHEET (illustrative formulas used in analysis):
- Revenue_delta = Price_change_pct * Elasticity_factor * Volume_base
- Compute_cost_new = Compute_unit_cost * Volume_new * (1 - optimization_rate)
- Margin = (Revenue - Compute - CloudInfra - Headcount - OtherOpex) / Revenue

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS:
- Elasticity estimates are noisy; we need 2 controlled price experiments in US and EU self-serve to tighten elasticity to +/-0.04 by end of Q1.
- Potential procurement lead time for GPUs in a market spike (30-60 days) creates risk to SLA if we must buy capacity reactively.
- Interaction with Dedicated sales: large committed deals materially change trigger cadence (need separate flow chart).

NEXT STEPS / ACTION ITEMS (owner, due):
- Build two segmented price experiments (Nora) - due 2027-01-18
- Instrument cohort-level churn & ARPA dashboards for week-over-week reporting (Diego) - due 2026-12-10
- Validate GPU procurement lead times & preferred vendors (Evan) - due 2026-12-20
- Publish trimmed playbook to Confluence and link into hiring ops (Leah) - due 2026-12-07

Revision history: 2026-11-12 initial draft by Leah; 2026-11-19 added trigger thresholds and sensitivity table (Diego); 2026-12-02 updated annex formulas and next steps (Nora).
